One agent run, six steps

Watch an agent build a page with the pack.

Voyager Open Blocks is a free WordPress block pack that teaches an agent to read the site, check its markup and bind real data. Here is one run, in the order the pack's skill gives it.

The brief, given to the agent
Add the voyager-open/cta-band pattern to the end of the Services page. Rewrite the heading and the line of copy for that page, keep the click-to-call button bound to voyager/site-data phone_link, and validate the page with Block Runner before saving.
skills/voyager-open-blocks/SKILL.mdWordPress 6.9+Scroll to play ↓
Open in PlaygroundRead the source
ReadCheckBind
1Step 1Read

It reads the site before it writes anything.

Wesper collects the blocks this site registers, its theme tokens and the fields it can bind. The agent works from that file, not from what it remembers about WordPress.

$ npx wesper collect --wp-path ./public --out site.context.json $ npx wesper summarize site.context.json blocks · tokens · bindable fields
2Step 2Read

It picks a pattern from the catalog.

The get-catalog ability lists the pack's patterns, the named blocks inside each one and every bindable field with its exact args. The brief asks for a call to action, so it takes the CTA band.

GET voyager-open-blocks/get-catalog voyager-open/cta-band copy: Eyebrow, Heading, Bodyvoyager-open/proof-strip voyager-open/logo-marquee voyager-open/contact-section voyager-open/closing-cta
3Step 3Write

It places the pattern with this page's copy.

insert adds a copy of the pattern at the end of the page and rewrites its named blocks by label. The heading and the line now belong to the Services page.

POST voyager-open-blocks/insert {"post_id":42,"item":"voyager-open/cta-band","position":2,"mode":"copy", "copy":{"Eyebrow":"Emergency repairs","Heading":"Need a plumber today?","Body":"Licensed plumbers on call…"}}
4Step 4Check

It proves the markup is valid before it saves.

Every piece of markup insert returns goes through Block Runner in strict mode, against the site context from step 1. Exit 0 saves. Exit 1 means fix it and validate again.

$ npx block-runner validate page.html --strict --json --context site.context.json exit 0 valid, saved
5Step 5Bind

It binds the one value the pattern left open.

The click-to-call button already reads phone and phone_link from Site Data. The brief wants the company name above the heading, so the agent binds the eyebrow. bind refuses any args the catalog does not list.

POST voyager-open-blocks/bind {"post_id":42,"path":"2/0/0/0","attribute":"content", "source":"voyager/site-data","args":{"key":"company"}}
6Step 6Bind

Then it checks that every value arrived.

get-post-blocks reads the page back. Each binding reports resolved or fell back, with the reason and a preview of the value, so the agent proves the page instead of assuming it.

GET voyager-open-blocks/get-post-blocks company resolved “Example Co.” phone resolved “(555) 010-0199” phone_link resolved “tel:5550100199”

Run the same build on your site.

Install the plugin on the site and the skills in the agent's harness, then give it the brief above. The five abilities also reach the pack over MCP.

  1. Add the skills to your agentnpx skills add voyager-marketing/voyager-open-blocks
  2. Install the plugin on the sitewp plugin install voyager-open-blocks.zip --activate
  3. Read the site, then give it the briefnpx wesper collect --wp-path ./public --out site.context.json
